title: Fine-Tuning Embedding Models
summary: A general embedding model does not know what counts as similar in your domain. This lesson explains how sentence-embedding models are trained with contrastive loss and in-batch negatives, then fine-tunes a small one on a laptop CPU with sentence-transformers, adds Matryoshka training for smaller vectors, and measures the gain with retrieval metrics on held-out documents.
objectives: Explain how a bi-encoder turns token states into one normalised vector and size a small embedding model's training memory
Compute the InfoNCE (MultipleNegativesRankingLoss) loss for a small similarity matrix and explain why batch size and the scale matter
Build (anchor, positive) pairs and mined hard negatives while avoiding false negatives and train/test leakage
Fine-tune an embedding model with SentenceTransformerTrainer, optionally with MatryoshkaLoss, and compute the storage of truncated and quantised vectors
Compare a base and a tuned model with recall@k, MRR@10 and NDCG@10 computed by hand and with InformationRetrievalEvaluator
prerequisites: Sentence vectors, pooling and cosine similarity from [Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings), especially [static and contextual embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings/static-and-contextual). The contrastive loss is easier if you have seen [the CLIP loss](/learn/training-and-adaptation/multimodal/clip-contrastive-loss). Memory per parameter is from [Sizing your first run](/learn/fine-tuning/start-here/sizing-your-first-run); environment setup is in [Run fine-tuning yourself](/learn/fine-tuning/run-fine-tuning-yourself).
